statement: The function returns a result r and r = max({0} union {j - i | 0 <= i < j <= len(s) and the interval s[i..j) is k-valid}). An interval s[i..j) is k-valid when, for every byte c, the number of indices t with i <= t < j and s[t] = c is either 0 or at least k. Equivalently, no character occurs in s[i..j) with a positive frequency smaller than k.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail by arithmetic overflow, panic, or out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(s).
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r > 0, then r >= k.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r > 0, there exist indices i and j such that 0 <= i < j <= len(s), j - i = r, and s[i..j) is k-valid, meaning that for every byte c, the number of indices t with i <= t < j and s[t] = c is either 0 or at least k.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every interval [i,j) with 0 <= i < j <= len(s), if every byte occurring in s[i..j) occurs at least k times in that interval, then j - i <= r.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no interval [i,j) with 0 <= i < j <= len(s) such that every byte occurring in s[i..j) occurs at least k times in that interval.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = len(s).
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); 1 <= k <= 100000; and k = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); 1 <= k <= 100000; and k > len(s).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if r = len(s), then the whole string s is k-valid, i.e. for every byte c, the number of indices t with 0 <= t < len(s) and s[t] = c is either 0 or at least k.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 1 if k = 1, while r = 0 if k > 1.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); 1 <= k <= 100000; and len(s) = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = len(s) if k <= len(s), while r = 0 if k > len(s).
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); 1 <= k <= 100000; and all bytes of s are equal, i.e. for every i and j with 0 <= i < len(s) and 0 <= j < len(s), s[i] = s[j].

statement: For every slice s' of bytes such that len(s') = len(s), every byte of s' is an ASCII lowercase letter, and s' has the same equality pattern as s (for all 0 <= i < len(s) and 0 <= j < len(s), s[i] = s[j] if and only if s'[i] = s'[j]), if the function returns r on (s,k) and returns r' on (s',k), then r' = r.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: For every k1 and k2 with 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 100000, if longest_substring(s,k1) returns r1 and longest_substring(s,k2) returns r2, then r1 >= r2.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: For every i and j with 0 <= i <= j <= len(s), let t be the slice of length j - i with t[p] = s[i + p] for 0 <= p < j - i. If longest_substring(t,k) returns r_t and longest_substring(s,k) returns r, then r_t <= r.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.

statement: Let s_rev be the slice of length len(s) with s_rev[i] = s[len(s) - 1 - i] for 0 <= i < len(s). If longest_substring(s_rev,k) returns r_rev and longest_substring(s,k) returns r, then r_rev = r.
preconditions: 0 <= len(s) <= 10000; every byte of s is an ASCII lowercase letter, i.e. 97 <= s[i] <= 122 for every 0 <= i < len(s); and 1 <= k <= 100000.
